explanation: Charles Darwin worked out how they form: a reef grows around a volcanic island and keeps building upward as the island slowly sinks out of sight.

claims.text: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or island that encloses a lagoon.
An archipelago is a group of islands, an isthmus is a narrow strip of land joining larger areas, and a delta is land built up at a river mouth.
Charles Darwin proposed that an atoll forms when a coral reef around a sinking volcanic island keeps growing upward.
Deep drilling on atolls later confirmed Darwin's explanation.

evidence.restatement: An atoll is a ring of coral reef or reef islands enclosing a lagoon.
An archipelago is a group of islands, an isthmus a narrow neck of land joining two larger areas, and a delta land built from sediment at a river mouth.
Darwin's subsidence theory says a fringing reef round a sinking volcanic island keeps growing upward until only a ring of reef around a lagoon remains.
Drilling on Enewetak Atoll in the early 1950s passed through more than a kilometre of reef limestone to volcanic rock, confirming Darwin's theory.
